subject: Vocabulary
topic: One Word Substitution — Second Advanced Set (W10 B2)

questions.stem: A person who boasts about their own achievements and abilities.
questions.explanation: A is correct. A BRAGGART = a person who boasts or talks arrogantly about their own achievements. Trap: VAGRANT = a person with no fixed home who wanders; PEDANT = a person overly concerned with minor rules; RECLUSE = a person who lives in isolation.

B is correct. ENTOMOLOGY = the scientific study of insects (from Greek 'entomon' = insect). Trap: Ornithology = birds; Herpetology = reptiles and amphibians; Ichthyology = fish. SSC regularly tests this set of scientific disciplines.

questions.stem: An inscription carved on a tomb or grave to commemorate the deceased.
questions.explanation: C is correct. EPITAPH = an inscription carved on a gravestone or tomb in memory of the deceased. Trap: EPITOME = a perfect example or embodiment; EPIGRAM = a witty or clever saying; EPILOGUE = the conclusion of a literary work. All four share the 'epi-' prefix, making this a classic SSC vocabulary trap.

questions.stem: A system of government in which power is held by the wealthiest class.
questions.explanation: D is correct. PLUTOCRACY = government by the wealthy; rule by the richest (from Greek 'ploutos' = wealth). Trap: AUTOCRACY = rule by one person; THEOCRACY = rule by religious leaders or God's laws; BUREAUCRACY = government by departments of state/officials. All end in '-cracy' (rule/power) — this is a key vocabulary family tested by SSC.

questions.stem: An abnormal and intense fear of open or public spaces and crowds.
questions.explanation: C is correct. AGORAPHOBIA = fear of open, crowded or public places (from Greek 'agora' = public marketplace). Trap: ACROPHOBIA = fear of heights; CLAUSTROPHOBIA = fear of enclosed spaces; XENOPHOBIA = fear or dislike of strangers/foreigners. SSC tests all four phobia terms — memorise them as a group.

questions.stem: A person who withdraws from society and lives in solitude.
questions.explanation: B is correct. RECLUSE = a person who lives a solitary life and tends to avoid other people. Trap: NOMAD = a person who moves from place to place (not necessarily in isolation); VAGABOND = a person wandering from place to place without a fixed home; MISANTHROPE = a person who dislikes humanity (but doesn't necessarily live alone).

questions.stem: A story, poem, or picture in which characters and events represent larger abstract ideas or moral qualities.
questions.explanation: C is correct. ALLEGORY = a story or representation in which characters and events are symbols that stand for larger truths or moral qualities (e.g., Aesop's fables are allegories). Trap: ANALOGY = a comparison; ANECDOTE = a short, amusing story; ANTHOLOGY = a collection of literary works. The 'all-' prefix group is a common SSC trap.

questions.stem: The use of the same consonant sound at the beginning of closely connected words (e.g., 'Peter Piper picked a peck').
questions.explanation: D is correct. ALLITERATION = the repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of consecutive or closely connected words. Trap: ASSONANCE = repetition of vowel sounds (not consonants); ONOMATOPOEIA = words that imitate sounds (buzz, hiss); HYPERBOLE = deliberate exaggeration for emphasis.

questions.stem: The practice by those in power of favouring their relatives or close friends in job appointments, regardless of merit.
questions.explanation: B is correct. NEPOTISM = the practice of giving unfair advantages to relatives or close associates in business or politics. From Latin 'nepos' = nephew (historically, popes gave positions to their nephews). Trap: CRONYISM = similar but specifically favouring friends (not relatives); SYCOPHANCY = using flattery to gain favour; PLAGIARISM = copying someone's work and claiming it as one's own.

questions.stem: A doctor who specialises in diagnosing and treating diseases of the nervous system.
questions.explanation: C is correct. NEUROLOGIST = a doctor specialising in the nervous system (neuro- = nerve). Trap: ONCOLOGIST = cancer specialist; CARDIOLOGIST = heart specialist; ENDOCRINOLOGIST = hormone/gland specialist. This tests the medical specialist vocabulary that appears frequently in SSC Tier 2 vocabulary and reading comprehension sections.
